decisions.headline: The superproject has three submodules: can_server (NestJS), can_app (Expo), can_promo_site (Next.js)
Submodule URLs are relative (../can_server.git) and point at local bare repos created next to the superproject
can_server owns the API contract: it generates openapi/openapi.json from code, and can_app builds its typed client from that file. There is no shared-packages repo
Postgres 16 runs via docker compose (host port 5433), with Drizzle 0.45.x as the ORM
Package manager is npm. engines.node is >=24. There is no .nvmrc
NestJS 12 framework defaults: ESM, Vitest and oxlint, not the Jest + ESLint setup the brief assumed
can_app runs on Expo SDK 57 with gluestack v5 on UniWind. If Expo web breaks, it falls back to civic wrappers over React Native core
Verification happens on Expo web only. Native builds only have to bundle
can_promo_site is a Next 16 static export with plain CSS, system fonts, no forms, no analytics, and no third-party fetches
The promo site targets developers first. The hero goes frustration → promise → a call to action to the repo and its open questions
The spec is split into docs/spec/* files of 25KB or less. The constitution goes into docs/spec/constitution/. build_spec.md is removed after the split; it stays in git history
Slice 1 scope
Slice 1 has no live AI. It runs deterministic checks plus human review. The AI gateway exists behind a flag that is off
Sign-in is a 6-digit email code. In development, mail goes to Mailpit. Email addresses are encrypted at rest and never shown. Handles are generated, and web uses an httpOnly cookie
Lifecycle changes

The initiator acts as provisional steward, and a moderator confirms publish, solved, closed and redirected. An interim-moderator clause makes these decisions audited, labelled interim, and re-reviewed once panels exist
Every moderation decision must carry rule_ids, a field or span reference, a revision hint, and appealable_until
Rejected or withdrawn drafts are hard-deleted after 30 days. A salted fingerprint is kept for 90 days to catch reposts
Constitution
"Hall of fame" is renamed "Resolution records", and "case" becomes "problem" throughout
Decentralization in slice 1 is limited to UUIDv7 IDs, origin_node_id, protocol_version, and append-only events with a nullable prev_hash. Signing, export and AT Protocol are deferred to the D-track
Open questions are treated as community work and tracked in docs/open-questions/, one file per question with its current default
Renamed can_promo_site to can_gallery
Hosted on GitHub (public) under community-action-network-oss
License: MIT for all four repos (code and docs)
Design system: gluestack-ui for all surfaces (can_app and can_gallery)
Core model: community-legislated, AI-executed moderation (founder)
Policy lives in a new 5th repo, can_policy (founder)
Slice 1 builds the full AI pipeline (founder), but this wave changes plans and design only
The repo is the single source of truth for CAN's design (founder)
The slice-1 proof is an AI persona simulation (founder)
Seed problems use the four real framings, with synthetic evidence (founder)
Hosting stays undecided, but every service must be portable (founder)
All content is structured (founder)
Retroactive re-resolution (founder)
The gallery asks everyone to contribute (founder)
Every moderation run applies a legal layer stack (founder)
OpenRouter is the model provider, free and cheap models first, chosen by eval (founder)
The gallery renders CAN's documents publicly (founder)
Gallery documents are fetched live in the browser (founder)
The gallery never shows a stale copy of a document (founder). Amends D-67
Visitors' IPs reaching GitHub is an accepted platform dependency, not a goal (founder)
Lifecycle redesign: preparation, volunteer review, AI publication, then a per-problem stage plan (founder)
Each contribution is labelled impacted or guest, using a private location attestation (founder)
Archive and reuse is CAN's second main goal (founder)
News watch: CAN problems follow the news, with Mera News as the first news pipeline partner behind a port (founder)
CAN for everyone: a gallery anyone can read, gradual unfolding, and the private capability profile (founder)
Night run 2026-10-02: defaults taken by unit agents (orchestrator log, for founder review)
Two cross-repo contracts settled before the 2026-10-03 night run (orchestrator default, for founder review)
